70	def _prepare_defaults(columns, normalizing=frozenset(), casefolding=frozenset()):
71	    """Validate the optional target-typed ``default`` of each column.
72	
73	    Returns a mapping of output field name to the processed default
74	    (string defaults are trimmed; a string column opting into NFKC also
75	    has its default NFKC-normalized and re-trimmed, and a string column
76	    opting into case folding then has it casefolded, in that order). A
77	    malformed default is a configuration error naming the default value
78	    and output field, raised before the input is read; the caller's
79	    schema dicts are never mutated. A normalized string default that
80	    becomes blank is refused here so the later ``allowed_values``
81	    membership check keeps using the final emitted text.
82	    """
83	    defaults = {}
84	    for column in columns:
85	        name, kind = column["name"], column["type"]
86	        if "default" not in column:
87	            continue
88	        default = column["default"]
89	        if kind == "string":
90	            if not isinstance(default, str):
91	                raise ValueError(f"column {name!r} default {default!r} must be a string")
92	            processed = default.strip()
93	            if not processed:
94	                raise ValueError(f"column {name!r} default {default!r} must not be blank")
95	            if name in normalizing:
96	                processed = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", processed).strip()
97	                if not processed:
98	                    raise ValueError(
99	                        f"column {name!r} default {default!r} must not normalize to blank")
100	            if name in casefolding:
101	                # Case folding never blanks a non-blank string, so the
102	                # folded default needs no further emptiness check.
103	                processed = processed.casefold()
104	            defaults[name] = processed
105	        elif kind == "integer":
106	            if isinstance(default, bool) or not isinstance(default, int):
107	                raise ValueError(
108	                    f"column {name!r} default {default!r} must be a non-boolean integer")
109	            defaults[name] = default
110	        else:
111	            if not isinstance(default, bool):
112	                raise ValueError(f"column {name!r} default {default!r} must be a boolean")
113	            defaults[name] = default
114	    return defaults

117	def _enum_field_error(name, value, allowed):
118	    """Return the enum error for a converted value, or None when it is allowed.
119	
120	    Null is never checked: an empty optional without a default stays null
121	    and membership is decided after type conversion and empty handling.
122	    """
123	    values = allowed.get(name)
124	    if values is not None and value is not None and value not in values:
125	        return f"{name}: value {value!r} is not one of allowed_values {values!r}"
126	    return None

129	def _prepare_allowed_values(columns, defaults):
130	    """Validate the optional ``allowed_values`` list of each column.
131	
132	    Returns a mapping of output field name to a fresh list holding the
133	    declared entries verbatim (strings are neither trimmed nor case
134	    folded). The attribute must be a non-empty list of target-typed
135	    values: strings for ``string`` columns, non-boolean integers for
136	    ``integer`` columns, booleans for ``boolean`` columns; null, arrays
137	    and objects are never valid entries, and repeated entries (value
138	    equality, verbatim for strings) are refused. A processed default
139	    outside the list is a configuration error even when no row needs it.
140	    Raises ValueError naming ``allowed_values`` and the output field
141	    before the input is read; the caller's schema is never mutated.
142	    """
143	    allowed = {}
144	    for column in columns:
145	        name, kind = column["name"], column["type"]
146	        if "allowed_values" not in column:
147	            continue
148	        values = column["allowed_values"]
149	        if not isinstance(values, list) or not values:
150	            raise ValueError(
151	                f"column {name!r} allowed_values {values!r} must be a non-empty list")
152	        checked = []
153	        for entry in values:
154	            if kind == "string":
155	                if not isinstance(entry, str):
156	                    raise ValueError(
157	                        f"column {name!r} allowed_values entry {entry!r} must be a string")
158	            elif kind == "integer":
159	                if isinstance(entry, bool) or not isinstance(entry, int):
160	                    raise ValueError(
161	                        f"column {name!r} allowed_values entry {entry!r} "
162	                        "must be a non-boolean integer")
163	            elif not isinstance(entry, bool):
164	                raise ValueError(
165	                    f"column {name!r} allowed_values entry {entry!r} must be a boolean")
166	            if entry in checked:
167	                raise ValueError(
168	                    f"column {name!r} allowed_values entry {entry!r} is repeated")
169	            checked.append(entry)
170	        allowed[name] = checked
171	        if name in defaults and defaults[name] not in checked:
172	            raise ValueError(
173	                f"column {name!r} default {defaults[name]!r} is not one of "
174	                f"allowed_values {checked!r}")
175	    return allowed

178	def _prepare_ranges(columns, defaults):
179	    """Validate the optional ``minimum``/``maximum`` bounds of each column.
180	
181	    Returns a mapping of output field name to a ``(minimum, maximum)``
182	    pair, with None for an unset end; either end may be declared alone
183	    and equal ends accept exactly that one integer. Bounds may appear
184	    only on ``integer`` columns and each must be a non-boolean integer
185	    (negative values and zero are legal): null, strings, floats and
186	    booleans are configuration errors, as is a minimum greater than the
187	    maximum. A processed default outside the declared range is a
188	    configuration error even when no row needs it. Raises ValueError
189	    naming the output field, the attribute and the offending value
190	    before the input is read; the caller's schema is never mutated.
191	    """
192	    ranges = {}
193	    for column in columns:
194	        name, kind = column["name"], column["type"]
195	        bounds = {}
196	        for attribute in ("minimum", "maximum"):
197	            if attribute not in column:
198	                continue
199	            bound = column[attribute]
200	            if kind != "integer":
201	                raise ValueError(
202	                    f"column {name!r} {attribute} {bound!r} requires an integer column")
203	            if isinstance(bound, bool) or not isinstance(bound, int):
204	                raise ValueError(
205	                    f"column {name!r} {attribute} {bound!r} must be a non-boolean integer")
206	            bounds[attribute] = bound
207	        if not bounds:
208	            continue
209	        minimum = bounds.get("minimum")
210	        maximum = bounds.get("maximum")
211	        if minimum is not None and maximum is not None and minimum > maximum:
212	            raise ValueError(
213	                f"column {name!r} minimum {minimum!r} is greater than "
214	                f"maximum {maximum!r}")
215	        if name in defaults:
216	            default = defaults[name]
217	            if minimum is not None and default < minimum:
218	                raise ValueError(
219	                    f"column {name!r} default {default!r} is less than "
220	                    f"minimum {minimum!r}")
221	            if maximum is not None and default > maximum:
222	                raise ValueError(
223	                    f"column {name!r} default {default!r} is greater than "
224	                    f"maximum {maximum!r}")
225	        ranges[name] = (minimum, maximum)
226	    return ranges

229	def _range_field_error(name, value, ranges):
230	    """Return the range error for a converted value, or None when in range.
231	
232	    Null is never checked: an empty optional without a default stays null
233	    and the inclusive bounds only see non-null integers, after type
234	    conversion, empty handling and the enum check.
235	    """
236	    bounds = ranges.get(name)
237	    if bounds is None or value is None:
238	        return None
239	    minimum, maximum = bounds
240	    if minimum is not None and value < minimum:
241	        return f"{name}: value {value!r} is less than minimum {minimum!r}"
242	    if maximum is not None and value > maximum:
243	        return f"{name}: value {value!r} is greater than maximum {maximum!r}"
244	    return None

247	def _pattern_field_error(name, value, patterns):
248	    """Return the pattern error for a converted value, or None when it matches.
249	
250	    Null is never checked: an empty optional without a default stays null
251	    and the full-string match only sees non-null strings, after type
252	    conversion, empty handling and the enum check. A matching value keeps
253	    its final text verbatim; the expression is the declared one, compiled
254	    with Python's standard ``re`` semantics (case-sensitive by default,
255	    inline flags honored).
256	    """
257	    compiled = patterns.get(name)
258	    if compiled is None or value is None:
259	        return None
260	    if compiled.fullmatch(value) is None:
261	        return (f"{name}: value {value!r} does not match pattern "
262	                f"{compiled.pattern!r}")
263	    return None

266	def _lte_field_errors(record, field_errors, lte_fields):
267	    """Check every declared ``lte_field`` relation over final integers.
268	
269	    Runs after structure checks, marker matching, default filling, type
270	    conversion, enum and range checks. A relation is skipped when either
271	    final value is null or either participating field already has a
272	    required, type, enum or range error; the original errors are kept and
273	    every other relation is still checked. Relations are evaluated in
274	    schema column order and returned as ``(name, message)`` pairs so the
275	    caller can file each error under its declaring column's position; a
276	    violation names ``lte_field``, both output names and the two actual
277	    integers (the local value larger than the target value fails;
278	    equality is legal).
279	    """
280	    errors = []
281	    for name, target in lte_fields:
282	        if name in field_errors or target in field_errors:
283	            continue
284	        local = record.get(name)
285	        other = record.get(target)
286	        if local is None or other is None:
287	            continue
288	        if local > other:
289	            errors.append((
290	                name,
291	                f"{name}: value {local!r} is greater than lte_field "
292	                f"{target!r} value {other!r}"))
293	    return errors

296	def _required_when_field_errors(record, field_errors, required_when):
297	    """Check every declared ``required_when`` condition over final values.
298	
299	    Runs after structure checks, marker matching, default filling, type
300	    conversion and the enum, range, pattern and lte_field checks. A
301	    condition is skipped when either participating field already carries
302	    an error; the original errors are kept and every other condition on
303	    the row is still checked. Conditions are evaluated in schema column
304	    order and returned as ``(name, message)`` pairs so the caller can
305	    file each error under its declaring column's position. The rule
306	    fires only when the condition column's final boolean is true and the
307	    declaring column's final value is null -- a false or null condition
308	    never fires, and a final 0 or false on the declaring column counts
309	    as a value. A violation names ``required_when``, both output names
310	    and the true condition value.
311	    """
312	    errors = []
313	    for name, target in required_when:
314	        if name in field_errors or target in field_errors:
315	            continue
316	        if record.get(target) is not True:
317	            continue
318	        if record.get(name) is not None:
319	            continue
320	        errors.append((
321	            name,
322	            f"{name}: value is null but required_when {target!r} is true"))
323	    return errors

326	def _prepare_lte_fields(columns):
327	    """Validate the optional ``lte_field`` reference of each integer column.
328	
329	    Returns a list of ``(name, target)`` pairs in schema column order, one
330	    entry per declaring column. The attribute must be a non-blank string
331	    naming another ``integer`` column by its output name (source aliases
332	    are not recognized); a non-string, a blank string, an unknown field,
333	    a self reference, a non-integer target, or declaring ``lte_field`` on
334	    a non-integer column is a configuration error. Raises ValueError
335	    naming ``lte_field``, the output field and the attribute value before
336	    the input is read; the caller's schema is never mutated.
337	    """
338	    by_name = {column["name"]: column for column in columns}
339	    lte_fields = []
340	    for column in columns:
341	        name, kind = column["name"], column["type"]
342	        if "lte_field" not in column:
343	            continue
344	        target = column["lte_field"]
345	        if not isinstance(target, str):
346	            raise ValueError(
347	                f"column {name!r} lte_field {target!r} must be a string naming "
348	                "an integer column")
349	        if not target.strip():
350	            raise ValueError(
351	                f"column {name!r} lte_field {target!r} must be a non-blank string")
352	        if kind != "integer":
353	            raise ValueError(
354	                f"column {name!r} lte_field {target!r} requires an integer column")
355	        if target == name:
356	            raise ValueError(
357	                f"column {name!r} lte_field {target!r} must not reference the column itself")
358	        if target not in by_name:
359	            raise ValueError(
360	                f"column {name!r} lte_field {target!r} is not a schema column name")
361	        if by_name[target]["type"] != "integer":
362	            raise ValueError(
363	                f"column {name!r} lte_field {target!r} must reference an integer column")
364	        lte_fields.append((name, target))
365	    return lte_fields

413	    """Validate the optional ``pattern`` regular expression of each column.
414	
415	    Returns a mapping of output field name to the compiled expression; the
416	    declared expression text is kept verbatim (``compiled.pattern`` hands
417	    it back) and the match later covers the whole string under Python's
418	    standard ``re`` semantics -- case-sensitive by default, with inline
419	    flags such as ``(?i)`` honored. The attribute must be a non-blank
420	    string and may appear only on a ``string`` column; a non-string or
421	    whitespace-only value, a declaration on an ``integer`` or ``boolean``

423	    configuration error. A processed ``default`` (already trimmed and, for
424	    an NFKC column, normalized) that does not match is a configuration

426	    that fails the expression is not. Raises ValueError naming
427	    ``pattern``, the output field and the offending value (the default
428	    error also names ``default``) before the input is read; the caller's
429	    schema is never mutated.

431	    patterns = {}
432	    for column in columns:
433	        name, kind = column["name"], column["type"]
434	        if "pattern" not in column:

547	    """Validate the structural shape of the schema before any file is read.
548

550	    each column must be an object carrying ``name`` (a non-blank string,

552	    ``type`` (one of ``string``, ``integer``, ``boolean``), plus an

555	    structure, name, duplicate name, type, required) and only the first
556	    problem is reported: the ValueError message names ``schema`` and the
557	    one-based column position, names a missing key, carries the
558	    offending value verbatim, and points a duplicate name at the later
559	    column. Unknown attributes are ignored and the caller's schema is
560	    never mutated.

563	        raise ValueError(f"schema must be an object, got {schema!r}")
564	    if "columns" not in schema:

568	        raise ValueError(f"schema 'columns' must be a non-empty list, got {columns!r}")

571	        if not isinstance(column, dict):

573	        for key in ("name", "type"):

576	        name = column["name"]

580	        if name in seen:

584	        kind = column["type"]

588	                "'string', 'integer', 'boolean'")

714	        details = []

716	        extra = sorted(keys - {"field", "value"})
717	        if missing:

719	        if extra:
720	            details.append("unexpected key(s): " + ", ".join(extra))

722	    field = filter_eq["field"]

807	def _deduplicate_records(records, deduplicate_by):
808	    """Keep the first record of each equal-key group, in input order.
809	
810	    Two records collide only when every named field's final value is
811	    equal (strings case-sensitively, null equal to null). The first
812	    record in input order is kept complete -- non-key fields are never
813	    merged or overwritten -- and the remaining records keep their
814	    relative order. Returns (kept, removed_count).
815	    """
816	    seen_keys = set()
817	    kept = []
818	    for record in records:
819	        key = tuple(record[field] for field in deduplicate_by)
820	        if key in seen_keys:
821	            continue
822	        seen_keys.add(key)
823	        kept.append(record)
824	    return kept, len(records) - len(kept)

827	def _build_result(records, errors, duplicate_fields, filter_condition,
828	                  deduplicate_fields=None, filter_in_condition=None):
829	    """Filter fully validated records, then keep-first dedup, then counts.
830	
831	    Order is: validation (already done by the caller), ``filter_eq`` and
832	    ``filter_in`` (a record survives only when every enabled predicate
833	    matches, so the two combine as AND; ``filtered`` counts each removed
834	    record once), keep-first deduplication over the filter survivors, and
835	    finally the duplicate report over the records that remain.
836	    """
837	    filtering = filter_condition is not None or filter_in_condition is not None
838	    filtered_records = records
839	    if filtering:
840	        eq_field, eq_expected = (
841	            filter_condition if filter_condition is not None else (None, None))
842	        in_field, in_values = (
843	            filter_in_condition if filter_in_condition is not None else (None, None))
844	
845	        def matches(record):
846	            if filter_condition is not None and record[eq_field] != eq_expected:
847	                return False
848	            if filter_in_condition is not None and record[in_field] not in in_values:
849	                return False
850	            return True
851	
852	        filtered_records = [record for record in records if matches(record)]
853	        filtered_count = len(records) - len(filtered_records)
854	    else:
855	        filtered_count = 0
856	    if deduplicate_fields is None:
857	        kept, deduplicated_count = filtered_records, 0
858	    else:
859	        kept, deduplicated_count = _deduplicate_records(
860	            filtered_records, deduplicate_fields)
861	    result = {"records": kept, "errors": errors, "accepted": len(kept),
862	              "rejected": len(errors)}
863	    if filtering:
864	        result["filtered"] = filtered_count
865	    if deduplicate_fields is not None:
866	        result["deduplicated"] = deduplicated_count
867	    if duplicate_fields is not None:
868	        result["duplicates"] = _find_duplicates(kept, duplicate_fields)

1228	def _csv_cell(value, quote_empty=False):
1229	    """Serialize one normalized value to a single CSV cell.
1230	
1231	    Integers are decimal text (booleans, checked first, are lowercase
1232	    ``true``/``false``), null is an empty cell, and strings keep their
1233	    normalized content including any embedded CR/LF characters. The same
1234	    quoting rule applies to every cell (headers included): a cell that
1235	    contains a comma, double quote, CR or LF is wrapped in double quotes
1236	    with each interior double quote doubled. An empty cell stays bare,
1237	    except in a single-column table (``quote_empty``), where it must be a
1238	    quoted empty string so the row cannot collapse into a skipped blank
1239	    line; every other cell stays unquoted.
1240	    """
1241	    if value is None:
1242	        text = ""
1243	    elif isinstance(value, bool):
1244	        text = "true" if value else "false"
1245	    elif isinstance(value, int):
1246	        text = str(value)
1247	    else:
1248	        text = value
1249	    if text == "" and not quote_empty:
1250	        return text
1251	    if text == "" or any(char in text for char in (",", '"', "\r", "\n")):
1252	        return '"' + text.replace('"', '""') + '"'
1253	    return text

1258

1262	    and the final record (an empty result still yields the header alone).

1272	def _stage_output(destination, payload):
1273	    """Serialize payload text into a temp file in the destination's directory.

1280	    parent = target.parent

1282	        raise OSError(f"cannot write {target}: parent directory does not exist")

1284	        raise OSError(f"cannot write {target}: target is a directory")

1289	            prefix=f".{target.name}.", suffix=".tmp", dir=parent)
1290	    except OSError as exc:
1291	        raise OSError(f"cannot write {target}: {exc}") from None
1292	    staged = parent / staged_name
1293	    try:
1294	        out = os.fdopen(handle, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="")
1295	    except BaseException:
1296	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
1297	            os.close(handle)

1315	def _install_staged(target, staged, existed):
1316	    """Replace target with staged, keeping its old bytes recoverable.
1317	
1318	    Returns the backup path (or None). If the swap fails after the
1319	    original was moved aside, the original is restored at target before
1320	    the OSError (naming target) is raised.
1321	    """
1322	    mode = None
1323	    backup = None
1324	    try:
1325	        if existed:
1326	            mode = target.stat().st_mode & 0o7777
1327	            # Reserve a unique backup name so an unrelated user file can
1328	            # never be clobbered; os.replace below overwrites the empty
1329	            # placeholder with the original file.
1330	            backup_handle, backup_name = tempfile.mkstemp(
1331	                prefix=f".{target.name}.", suffix=".backup", dir=target.parent)
1332	            os.close(backup_handle)
1333	            backup = target.parent / backup_name
1334	            os.replace(target, backup)
1335	        os.replace(staged, target)
1336	        if mode is not None:
1337	            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
1338	                target.chmod(mode)
1339	        else:
1340	            # mkstemp creates 0600; a freshly created output historically
1341	            # got the usual 0666 & ~umask mode from open().
1342	            umask = os.umask(0)
1343	            os.umask(umask)
1344	            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
1345	                target.chmod(0o666 & ~umask)
1346	    except OSError as exc:
1347	        if backup is not None:
1348	            if target.exists():
1349	                # The original never left target; just drop the placeholder.
1350	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
1351	                    backup.unlink()
1352	            else:
1353	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
1354	                    os.replace(backup, target)
1355	        raise OSError(f"cannot write {target}: {exc}") from None
1356	    return backup

1360	    """Write both output files as one all-or-nothing operation.

1362	    Either both files are fully written (replacing existing files), or a
1363	    filesystem failure leaves every target exactly as it was beforehand:
1364	    pre-existing files keep their bytes and previously absent files stay
1365	    absent. Parent directories are never created. The records output
1366	    carries output_payload (JSONL or CSV text); the errors output is
1367	    always JSONL.

1371	        for record in errors)
1372	    output_target, errors_target = Path(output_path), Path(errors_path)
1373	    staged_output, output_existed = _stage_output(output_target, output_payload)
1374	    try:
1375	        staged_errors, errors_existed = _stage_output(errors_target, errors_payload)
1376	    except BaseException:
1377	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
1378	            staged_output.unlink()
1379	        raise
1380	    installs = []
1381	    try:
1382	        installs.append((output_target,
1383	                         _install_staged(output_target, staged_output, output_existed)))
1384	        installs.append((errors_target,
1385	                         _install_staged(errors_target, staged_errors, errors_existed)))
1386	    except BaseException:
1387	        # Undo only fully completed installs; a failed _install_staged

1396	            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):

1405	def _check_path_isolation(source, schema, output, errors):
1406	    """Reject when an output aliases an input or the other output.
1407	
1408	    Runs before either input is read or either output is written. Two
1409	    paths alias when their resolved pathnames are equal (identical paths,
1410	    including relative/absolute spellings and symbolic-link aliases) or,
1411	    when both paths currently exist, when they share a device and inode
1412	    (distinct hard links to the same file). Outputs that do not exist yet
1413	    only take part in the pathname comparison, so two fresh names are not
1414	    refused merely because they could later be linked together. File
1415	    names, extensions and directories never decide identity, and two
1416	    independent files with identical contents are always allowed. Any I/O
1417	    error resolving or stating a path propagates as OSError naming it.
1418	    """
1419	    roles = (
1420	        ("source", Path(source)),
1421	        ("schema", Path(schema)),
1422	        ("records output", Path(output)),
1423	        ("errors output", Path(errors)),
1424	    )
1425	
1426	    def resolve(path):
1427	        try:
1428	            return path.resolve()
1429	        except OSError as exc:
1430	            raise OSError(f"cannot check path {path}: {exc}") from None
1431	
1432	    def file_identity(labeled_path, resolved):
1433	        try:
1434	            result = resolved.stat()
1435	        except FileNotFoundError:
1436	            return None
1437	        except OSError as exc:
1438	            raise OSError(f"cannot check path {labeled_path}: {exc}") from None
1439	        return result.st_dev, result.st_ino
1440	
1441	    entries = [(label, path, resolve(path)) for label, path in roles]
1442	    # Pairs involving at least one output, in a fixed order: the two
1443	    # outputs, then records output against the inputs, then errors output.
1444	    pairs = ((2, 3), (2, 0), (2, 1), (3, 0), (3, 1))
1445	    for left_index, right_index in pairs:
1446	        left_label, left_path, left_resolved = entries[left_index]
1447	        right_label, right_path, right_resolved = entries[right_index]
1448	        if left_resolved == right_resolved:
1449	            raise ValueError(
1450	                f"paths must be distinct: {left_label} {left_path} and "
1451	                f"{right_label} {right_path} point to the same file")
1452	        left_identity = file_identity(left_path, left_resolved)
1453	        right_identity = file_identity(right_path, right_resolved)
1454	        # A not-yet-existing path (or a dangling link to one) cannot
1455	        # currently be hard-linked to an existing file; the resolved
1456	        # pathname comparison above still applies to both spellings.
1457	        if left_identity is None or right_identity is None:
1458	            continue
1459	        if left_identity == right_identity:
1460	            raise ValueError(
1461	                f"paths must be distinct: {left_label} {left_path} and "
1462	                f"{right_label} {right_path} point to the same existing file")
